name: 1969 NI Parliament
provider: Interim Boundary Commission for Northern Ireland
description: The 52 territorial constituencies of the Parliament of Northern Ireland used at the 1969 general election. Forty-two seats are unchanged from 1929 and keep the 1929 lines. Ten seats in Co. Antrim and Co. Down were redrawn, four of them new (Bangor, Lagan Valley, Larkfield and Newtownabbey), following the map of proposed constituencies in the Interim Boundary Commission for Northern Ireland's 1967 report. The redrawn seats are built from whole 1930 district electoral divisions where the map moves whole divisions; four divisions split by the proposal (Ballygomartin, Ballyduff, Monkstown and Crawfordsburn) were cut along the map's line, accurate to about 150 m. The Bangor seat follows the borough as extended on 1 April 1967, plus Groomsport. The composition is read from the Commission's proposal map and assumes that the Electoral Law Act (Northern Ireland) 1968 enacted the proposals unchanged; the Act's schedule has not been checked. The Commission's population and electorate figures for the redrawn seats are included. The Queen's University seats had no territory and are not shown.

references.label: Interim Boundary Commission for Northern Ireland, Report (1967): map showing proposed constituencies and summary of proposals
references.note: Source of the redrawn seats and of the population and electorate figures. The Commission was appointed by warrant of 31 January 1967; its map showing existing constituencies was used as a check against the 1929 layer.

references.label: Electoral Law Act (Northern Ireland) 1968
references.note: Gave effect to the new constituencies for the 1969 general election. Assumed to follow the Commission's proposals unchanged; the schedule has not been compared.

references.label: Bangor Borough (Extension) Order (Northern Ireland) 1966
references.note: Bangor borough as extended from 1 April 1967, used for the Bangor/North Down line.
